about.intro: Pattes Douces is a community blog where pets, with a little help from their humans, share their adventures, comment and react.
about.body: It started as a student project and remains open: its source code is public and anyone can suggest improvements.
about.sourceLink: See the source code on GitHub

contact.intro: A question, a bug, a remark about accessibility? Write to us by opening an issue on GitHub: we answer within a few days.

privacy.intro: Pattes Douces only collects what the blog needs to work. No ads, no trackers, no third-party cookies.
privacy.account: Username, email address, bio and species. Your password is hashed (bcrypt): nobody, not even us, can read it.
privacy.content: Your articles, images, comments, reactions and the articles you have read. Images are hosted by Vercel Blob.
privacy.browser: Your session and theme choice are kept in your browser’s local storage; your language in a technical cookie (NEXT_LOCALE).
privacy.translation: Articles and comments are translated in your browser when it can do so (Chrome): the text never leaves your device. Otherwise, the “Translate with Google Translate” link opens the text on Google’s website, which receives it.
privacy.deletion: From your profile, “Delete account” erases your account, your articles and your comments.

accessibility.intro: Pattes Douces is committed to making its website accessible, following the French accessibility framework RGAA version 4.1.2, which matches WCAG 2.2 level AA.
accessibility.status: Pattes Douces is partially compliant with RGAA 4.1.2: the October 2026 redesign was built to meet level AA, but no full audit has been carried out yet.
accessibility.tests: Automated tests (axe, Lighthouse), keyboard-only journeys, tests at 320 px wide, at 200% and 400% zoom and in Arabic (right-to-left) have been carried out. An RGAA audit on a sample of pages is planned.
limits: Article images have no text alternative of their own: authors are invited to describe them in the article text.
Content published by members may not follow every rule (structure, language).
Screen reader tests (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver, TalkBack) are still to be carried out.
accessibility.date: This statement was made on 19 October 2026.
accessibility.contact: If you cannot access a piece of content or a service, contact us so we can direct you to an accessible alternative or provide the content in another form.
accessibility.remedy: If you notice an accessibility issue that prevents you from accessing content, have reported it to us and have not received a satisfactory answer, you can contact the French Defender of Rights (Défenseur des droits): through its online form, or by free mail to Défenseur des droits, Libre réponse 71120, 75342 Paris CEDEX 07, France.
